summary: Read a square character grid whose side length is between 1 and 30. Each cell holds one of three symbols: a forward slash, a backslash, or a space. A slash splits its cell into smaller pieces, while a space leaves that cell whole. Two pieces belong to the same region whenever they share a border of positive length. Count how many separate regions the lines carve across the whole grid, and write that count.
notes: The left column is this sample's input text and the right column is the text the program should print. Comparison ignores trailing newlines.
